claim: Speaker-relative prosody can improve affective-state prediction while suppressing stable speaker-trait information.
key_result: Pitch Relative−Absolute: emotion +0.059 to +0.091 Macro-F1 across ESD/MEAD/RAVDESS; gender −0.133 to −0.379.
limitation: Gender is a strong trait example; speaker identity suppression is only modest (EXP-20260921-11).

claim: Reference-frame preference depends on the target reference frame, not on a universally superior normalization.
status: Strong MSP confirmation; directional external support
key_result: MSP speaker-cluster slopes are significantly negative under linear/quadratic Ridge; IEMOCAP point slopes are also negative but slope CIs cross zero with only 10 speakers. Pure within-speaker endpoints favor Relative in both corpora.
limitation: IEMOCAP slope inference is low-powered at the speaker level; do not describe it as independently significant.

claim: Pure within-speaker affect targets consistently prefer Relative prosody.
key_result: At λ=0, all 8 corpus×target×model Arousal/Dominance cells have positive Relative−Absolute CCC.
limitation: Valence remains weak and does not show the same strong pattern.

claim: Stable speaker centers matter only when aligned to the correct speaker and when the target contains speaker-level structure.
key_result: MSP raw true-center vs permuted-center: +0.296 Arousal, +0.236 Dominance CCC; residual effects ≈+0.001.
limitation: IEMOCAP raw effects are much smaller because between-speaker VAD structure is weak.

claim: A small unlabeled enrollment set can recover useful speaker-reference information.
key_result: K=20 Hybrid is within 0.0043 CCC of marginal oracle for Arousal and essentially identical for Dominance on a fixed downstream pool.
limitation: Strict diminishing-return shape was not supported; K selection is corpus-dependent.

claim: The target-reference mechanism is not an artifact of one model family.
key_result: Negative Arousal/Dominance slopes persist under both linear and quadratic Ridge in both corpora.
limitation: Earlier class-level categorical effects are more classifier-sensitive (EXP-20260920-15).

claim: WavLM preserves information corresponding to multiple prosodic reference frames.
key_result: WavLM preserves multiple reference frames, and direct embedding-space intervention yields significantly negative Arousal/Dominance slopes at layers 12 and 24.
limitation: Full-speaker embedding centers are diagnostic oracle references; numerical-solver sensitivity is reported separately.

claim: IEMOCAP provides a clean loudness replication.
key_result: Replacing undocumented relative_db with RMS dB removed/reversed the loudness mechanism.
limitation: IEMOCAP loudness must be excluded from main evidence.

claim: Target-reference coupling extends beyond acoustic level features to expressive range and temporal/voicing structure.
key_result: F0 variability, pause ratio, voiced ratio, and their combined representation all show significantly negative Arousal/Dominance slopes; the combined λ=0 endpoint favors Relative.
limitation: This extension is currently validated on MSP rather than independently across multiple corpora.

claim: Target-reference matching survives speaker-level statistical inference.
key_result: MSP Arousal/Dominance slopes remain strongly negative under 1,915-speaker cluster bootstrap; IEMOCAP mean slopes remain negative but 10-speaker CIs cross zero.
limitation: IEMOCAP has only 10 speakers, so slope uncertainty remains large.

claim: Target-reference matching extends to learned SSL representation space.
key_result: WavLM layers 12/24 show 4/4 significantly negative Arousal/Dominance slopes and 4/4 positive lambda=0 Relative endpoints under speaker-cluster bootstrap.
limitation: Validated on IEMOCAP only so far; centers are diagnostic full-speaker centers.

claim: The mechanism extends beyond acoustic level features.
key_result: F0 variability, pause ratio, and voiced ratio all show significantly negative Arousal/Dominance slopes on MSP.
limitation: These extended attributes are currently validated on MSP only.
